full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Haque J: This appeal has arisen out of the leave granted by this Court on 9-2-2003 in Criminal Petition No. 19 of 2003 preferred by the appellant against the judgment and order dated 5-1-2003 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9916 of 2002 making the Rule absolute and enlarging the respondents on bail. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that in the night following 1-1-2002 one Alam, an industrialist was brutally killed along with 3 maid servants Kamala, Rahima and Sakina. A first information report was lodged with Shampur Police Station, being Shampur Police Station Case No.2 dated 2-1-2002 corresponding to GR Case No. 220 of2002. In the said first information report none of the accused persons were implicated. On the basis of the said first information report Sub-Inspector Delwar Hossain Chowdhury started investigation by visiting the place of occurrence, preparing sketch map, index and inquest report of the deceased and took other necessary steps. The said Sub-Inspector Delwar Hossain Chowdhury also recorded the statement of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and arrested some accused persons including Md Sohel, Sohag Bepari, Kabir and Jahanara Begum who made confessional statements which were duly recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. At this stage the case was handed over to Md Aktaruzzaman Bhuiyan. Assistant Commissioner, Detective Branch. DMP Dhaka by an order of the higher authority. During the investigation the said Assistant Commissioner, Detective Branch arrested 5(five) accused persons and recorded the statement of some other witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. One of the witnesses made a statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Ultimately, a final report was submitted in Shampur Police Station Case No. 2 dated 2-1-2002 on 18-7-2002 and it was accepted on 18-7-2002 by the learned Magistrate. Another first information report was lodged on the same date implicating the respondents and others in the 

 3. It appears that the accused respondents had filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3447 of 2002 arising out of Shampur Police Station Case No. 28 dated 18-7-2002 corresponding to GR No. 2938 of 2002 under sections 180(b)/302/380/ 201/212/114/411/134 of the Penal Code in the Court of Metropolitan Session Judge, Dhaka for bail. The said Session Judge, Dhaka after hearing rejected the prayer for bail by Order No.4 dated 5-10-2002. 

 4. The accused respondents being aggrieved by the aforesaid order dated 5-10-2002 of the said Session Judge, Dhaka moved the High Court Division for bail in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9916 of 2002 and the High Court Division granted bail to the accused respondents Md Matiur Rahman alias Matin and Md Ali Babul Hassan alias Babu Jamal mainly on the ground that the case is based on the circumstantial evidence and observed that from the materials on record no direct complicity of the accused respondents in the alleged occurrence was found. 

 5. The respondents herein stated that the informant after perusing the statements of the accused persons and witnesses came to learn that the deceased industrialist Mr Alam had 2(two) wives, 1st wife was blessed with 3(three) sons and I(one) daughter, and second wife was blessed with 4(four) daughters. They did not live with Mr Alam and deceased Alam lived in the 1st floor of 227 Alambagh of New Jurain under Shampur Police Station. The sons of the 1st wife of Mr Alam had been passing their days by independent business and Mr Alam appointed 1) Farida, 2) Monowara, 3) Kamola, 4) Sakhina, 5) Rahima as maid-servants and they all lived with him in the same house. They further stated that Farida was very much faithful to the deceased Mr Alam than other maid-servants in all respects and she took all the responsibility to look after the said house, even she kept all the keys of deceased Alam's house and the act of cooking and serving out meals was under the care of said Farida. However, an altercation and mutual ill feelings started between Farida and deceased Alam some days before the date of occurrence and as a result the said Farida was offended by deceased Mr Alam. On the other hand, due to detachment of the sons of 1st wife of the deceased Mr Alam, Md Motiur Rahman alias Matin and Md Ali Babul alias Babu Jamai, the 2(two) sons-in-law of the deceased Alam were engaged themselves with the business of deceased Mr Alam and they were enjoying with all financial facilities of the business institutions of deceased Mr Alam. When this fact was disclosed to deceased Alam, he called his 3(three) sons and handed over all responsibilities of his business institutions to them, and as a result Mr Alam's 2(two) sons-in-law became offended by him and that they in collusion with the maid-servant Farida were trying to kill Mr Alam and they conspired with each other and hired professional killer in lieu of big amount of money and on 1-1-2002 at mid night at 12.00 hours with the help of Farida the accused persons entered into Alam's house and attacked him (Alam) with deadly sharp weapons and killed Mr Alam, and 3(three) other maid-servants namely, Kamola, Rahima and Sakhina, who were trying to prevent the accused persons and thereafter, they opened the store room with the help of said Farida and looted cash money and took away by 2(two) big bags of jute and looted one bag of gold ornaments and wrist watch. The deceased industrialist Mr Alam had no estimate or any statement in respect of his cash money and gold ornaments, consequently the informant could not specify how much cash money and gold ornaments were looted by the accused persons and the informant mentioned in the ejahar in details about the recovered cash money and goods and hence the case. 

 6. It appears that the accused respondents were arrested by the police in connection with Sham pur Police Station Diary No. 270 dated 3-7-2002 under section 54(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and on 20-7-2002 were shown arrested in connection with the instant Criminal Case. It is the definite case of the respondents that there is no specific allegation of overt act against the respondents and they did not take any part in committing the alleged murder. They stated that they were compelled to make statements under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure implicating themselves in the instant case. They further stated that they are not involved in criminal case and they have been rightly enlarged on bail. 

 7. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division on 5-1-2002 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9916 of 2002 the present appellant as the petitioner filed Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 19 of 2003 before this Division and after hearing leave was granted by order dated 8-2-2003 to consider the following submissions: 

 "Mr Abdur Razaque Khan, the learned Additional Attorney-General appearing for the petitioner-State, seriously objects to the bail granted to the accused respondents by the High Court Division and submits that both the accused respondents are first information report named accused in Shampur Police Station Case No. 28(7) of 2002 under sections 102(b)/302/380/201/212/114/411/34 of the Penal Code and the informant of the said case is one Md Fazlur Rahman, Inspector of CID City Zone (East) who suo moto lodged the said first information report on the basis of the facts and circumstances and materials on record. 

 Lastly, he submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division mechanically passed the impugned order without considering the prima facie case as made out in the first information report and statements of witnesses under sections 161 and 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be set aside." 

 8. It appears that Motiur Rahman alias Matin intentionally by concealing his original plan lodged earlier first information report being Shampur Police Station Case No. 2(1) of 2002. It also appears that the accused petitioner Md Ali Babul Hasan alias Babu Jamai is a murderer and accused of Sham pur Police Station Case No.4 dated 16-11-1999 under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code which is now under trial in the Court of 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka being Sessions Case No. 1607 of 2000. It also appears that during investigation accused Md Ali Babul Hasan alias Babu Jamai, made a confessional statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on 29-12-2002. It has been submitted by the appellant that the accused Md Ali Babul Hasan alias Babu Jamai is a killer and after releasing on bail in the Sessions Case No. 1607 of 2000 has committed the self-same offence and, as such, the accused respondents should not be enlarged on bail. 

 9. It also appears that the accused respondents moved instant Criminal Miscellaneous Case under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure praying for bail and the Division Bench of the High Court Division issued Rule calling upon the present appellant to show cause as to why the respondents (petitioners) shall not be enlarged on bail. The said Criminal Miscellaneous Case was heard by a Division Bench of the High Court Division and after hearing both the parties the High Court Division were pleased to make the Rule absolute and enlarged the respondents on bail. 

 10. It has been submitted by the appellant that both the accused respondents are first information report named accused persons in the present case being Shampur Police Station Case No. 28(7) 2002 under sections 120(b)/302/380/201/212/114/411/34 of the Penal Code and the informant of the said case is one Md Fazlur Rahman, Inspector of cm City Zone(East) and he lodged suo moto first information report on the basis of the facts and circumstances and materials on record. It also appears that as many as 3(three) co-accused persons have made judicial confessional statements under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure implicating the respondents in the act of murder of Mr Alam. It has been submitted by the appellant that legality or otherwise of admissibility of statements of witnesses made under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure or confessional statements made under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure are not appropriately a matter for consideration at this stage of the trial. 

 11. It has further been submitted that the learned Judges of the High Court Division while entertaining and granting bail to the accused respondents did not consider that the present case against the accused persons is grave and serious in nature having clear and specific involvement of the accused respondents and that the respondents are first information report named accused persons. 

 13. Admitted position in this case is that 4(four) persons were brutally killed and there are very strong circumstantial evidence against the respondents besides confessional statements made by the 3(three) accused persons under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure implicating the respondents in the murder of Mr Alam. Over and above, the witnesses have made statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Further, the case is still under investigation. stage; therefore, there is hardly any scope to weigh the evidence that are available against the accused respondents; this is not a stage of trial to consider the legality or otherwise of admissibility of statements of witnesses made under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure or confessional statements made under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 14. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and specially when the case is at the investigation stage, the High Court Division ought not to have enlarged the respondents on bail. There was no occasion for the High Court Division to consider legality or otherwise of admissibility of statements of witnesses made under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure or judicial confession made under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as stated hereinabove; that there are strong circumstantial evidence against the accused respondents and we are of the view that the High Court Division has fallen in error in weighing the evidence which are already on record and enlarged the accused respondents on bail. The High Court Division ought not to have enlarged the accused persons on bail in such a gruesome murder of four persons. 

 Accordingly, the appeal succeeds. The judgment and order passed by the High Court Division dated 5-1-2003 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9916 of 2002 making the Rule absolute and granting bail, which has arisen out of Order No. 4 dated 5-10-2002 passed by the learned Chief Metropolitan Session Judge, Dhaka in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3447 of 2002 arising out of Shampur Police Station Case No. 28 dated 18-7-2002 corresponding to GR No. 2938 of 2002 under sections 120(b)/302/380/201/212/114/411/34 of the Penal Code, rejecting the prayer for bail now pending in the Court of learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, is hereby set aside.
